overview: Black answers 1.g4 with 1...g5, mirroring White. The most played continuation is 2.f4, the Coca-Cola Gambit, where White opens lines at the cost of a pawn, while quieter 2.Bg2 and 2.h3 simply fianchetto. Strong players hardly ever play it, so the picture is uncertain.

white_ideas.idea: Offer a pawn with f4 to open lines and attack g5
Fianchetto with Bg2 and aim at the long diagonal

black_ideas.idea: Capture on f4 and keep the extra pawn

typical_structures.structure: Open lines on the kingside after fxg5

character.notes: Both kings are weakened and 2.f4 opens the f-file at once, so play is unbalanced.

gambit.notes: 2.f4 gxf4 leaves White a pawn down for development and Black can keep it with care.

soundness.notes: The Grob is considered dubious for White, and the Coca-Cola Gambit is no exception.

structure.notes: The wings are active and the centre is undecided.

approach.notes: The Grob family is the standard example of an offbeat opening.

level.notes: Not a good choice for study.

sublines_that_differ.name: Quiet Double Grob
sublines_that_differ.how: White fianchettoes and plays a slow game.

character.reason: Both kings are weakened and the Coca-Cola Gambit opens the f-file at once.

gambit.reason: White gives a pawn with 2.f4 and Black can take it.

soundness.reason: Engines prefer Black and strong players avoid it.

structure.reason: The centre is undecided and the play is on the wings.

approach.reason: The Grob family is the textbook offbeat opening.

level.reason: A dubious line is never beginner, and it holds little to study.
